title: Open extension by zero and restriction for sheaf dg modules
statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A$ a sheaf dg $\mathcal O$-algebra, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use left sheaf dg modules and degree-zero chain maps as in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be open, with inclusion $j$, and write $\mathcal A_U=\mathcal A|_U$. For a left dg $\mathcal A_U$-module $L$, define a graded presheaf $P_L$ on $X$ by $P_L^q(V)=L^q(V)$ when $V\subseteq U$, and $P_L^q(V)=0$ otherwise. Its restrictions are those of $L$ when the source open is contained in $U$, and zero otherwise; the differential and the $\mathcal A(V)$-action are those of $L$ or zero. Sheafify each degree as an $\mathcal O$-module [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The resulting graded sheaf $j_!L$ has an induced differential and left $\mathcal A$-action, and these constructions on objects and maps define a functor on dg modules. There is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{dg}\,\mathcal A}(j_!L,M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{dg}\,\mathcal A_U}(L,M|_U)$$
for every left sheaf dg $\mathcal A$-module $M$. Both Hom sets here consist of degree-zero action-preserving chain maps, before passing to homotopy or inverting quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0FRW (lemma-extension-by-zero-dg), degree-zero closed maps, and Tag 0FRA (lemma-extension-by-zero-graded), specialized to the open site of a space; left-module convention. Explicit presheaf construction as in section-localize-graded and section-localize-dg.

proof.text: For each degree q form P_L^q as in the statement. For W subset V, the only case in which the source is nonzero is V subset U, and then W subset U too. Hence composable restrictions either are restrictions of L throughout or have zero source; this proves the presheaf identities and compatibility with d and the action. On V subset U the identities d^2=0, 1x=x, (ab)x=a(bx) and d(ax)=d(a)x+(-1)^{|a|}a d(x) are those of L; on every other V they are identities on zero modules. Thus P_L is a presheaf dg module in the explicit left convention of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization].

source.place: Tags 0FRI (definition-dgm), 0FRV (section-localize-dg); the explicit zero presheaf on the opens site

proof.text: Write J^q=(P_L^q)^# and eta_q:P_L^q -> J^q. The module-sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] extends eta_{q+1} d uniquely to D^q:J^q -> J^{q+1}. For each p,q the presheaf pairing A^p times P_L^q -> J^{p+q}, (a,x) |-> eta_{p+q}(ax), is O-bilinear and restriction-compatible. Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension] to obtain A^p times J^q -> J^{p+q}; here the sheafification of the already sheaf A^p is canonically A^p, since its identity has the sheafification universal property. This constructs the proposed differential and action, with D eta=eta d and a eta(x)=eta(ax).

These operations satisfy the dg-module laws. Indeed, [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-underlying-sets] identifies the underlying sets of J^q with set sheafification, and [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] says every section of J^q is locally eta_q(x). On such a representative the two sides of each law reduce, by the formulas in step 2, respectively to eta(d^2x)=0, eta(1x)=eta(x), eta((ab)x)=eta(a(bx)), and eta(d(ax))=eta(d(a)x+(-1)^p a d(x)). These are the identities of step 1. Sheaf separatedness makes the equalities global. Bilinearity was supplied in step 2, so this proves all axioms of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. No boundedness or exactness assertion is needed.

source.place: Tag 0FRV (section-localize-dg), omitted verification of differentials; local-section test from sites.tex Tag 00WK and sheaves.tex Tag 0087

proof.text: A dg map f:L -> L' gives the presheaf map P_f equal to f on opens inside U and to the zero map elsewhere. Sheafify degreewise using [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The induced map J_f satisfies J_f eta=eta P_f. Differential compatibility follows from the uniqueness of linear extensions in that node. Action compatibility follows from uniqueness of bilinear extension in [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension], since on A^p times P_L^q both composites are eta(f(ax))=eta(a f(x)). Identity and composition agree after each eta, hence agree by linear uniqueness. Consequently this is a functor on dg modules, denoted j_!. Restriction simply restricts every structure map and preserves its identities.

source.place: Tag 0FRV (section-localize-dg), functor on maps; Tags 03CY and 0GMW for the extension and uniqueness

proof.text: First ignore the differential and action. Degree by degree, [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] identifies O-linear maps g^q:J^q -> M^q with presheaf O-linear maps h^q:P_L^q -> M^q. Such h^q are in natural bijection with O_U-linear sheaf maps f^q:L^q -> M^q|_U: restrict h^q to opens contained in U; conversely set h_V^q=f_V^q for V subset U and h_V^q=0 otherwise. For W subset V, naturality holds by that of f if V subset U, and has zero source if V is not contained in U. The two recipes are inverse because the other source modules are zero. Taking these explicit inverses in every integer degree gives the bijection on graded underlying module maps, with f_V^q=g_V^q eta_{q,V} for V subset U.

source.place: Tag 0FRA (lemma-extension-by-zero-graded), underlying graded module adjunction; Tag 03CY for the explicit presheaf realization

proof.text: Under step 5, g is a chain map exactly when f is. Compare d_M g^q and g^{q+1}D^q: linear uniqueness of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] tests their equality after eta_q, where on opens inside U it reads d_M f^q=f^{q+1}d_L, and elsewhere the source is zero. Likewise compare the two bilinear maps A^p times J^q -> M^{p+q}, (a,z) |-> g(az) and (a,z) |-> a g(z). Uniqueness in [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension] tests equality on A^p times P_L^q; on opens inside U this reads f(ax)=a f(x), and elsewhere the second factor is zero. Thus the bijection restricts precisely to the degree-zero action-preserving chain maps of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. For precomposition by t:L' -> L its value on x is f(t(x)), since J_t eta=eta P_t; for postcomposition by s:M -> M' it is s(f(x)). This proves naturality in both variables and the asserted adjunction before homotopy or localization.
